[2 December, 2003] RAJYA SABHA  
RAJYA SABHA 
Tuesday, the 2nd December, 2003/11 Agrahayana, 1925 (Saka) 
The House met at eleven of the clock, MR. CHAIRMAN in the Chair. 
The National Anthem, "Jana Gana Mana" was played. 
MEMBERS SWORN 
Dr. Narayan Singh Manaklao (Nominated) 
Dr. Chandan Mitra (Nominated) 
WELCOME TO NEW MEMBERS 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, it  gives me great pleasure to 
congratulate and extend my warm welcome to the newly-elected and 
nominated Members, namely, Shnmati Kamla Manhar, Shri V. Narayanasamy, 
Shri Bimal Jalan, Shri Dara Singh, Shrimati Hema Malini, Dr. Chandan Mitra, 
Dr. K. Kasturirangan, Shri Vidya Niwas Misra and Dr. Narayan Singh 
Manaklao on behalf of this House and on my own behalf. Shri Narayansamy, 
who had been a Member of this House for two terms, is an old and familiar 
face. 
The new Members, I am sure, will soon acquaint themselves with the 
spirit and content of Parliamentary procedure and practice. We look forward to 
their valuable contribution in promoting and enhancing the dignity and 
prestige of this august House. 
I once again welcome the new Members and wish them success. 
OBITUARY REFERENCES 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the 
passing away of Shri Lalbuaia, Dr. A.  Subba Rao, former Members of this 
House, Shri K.M.Khan, a sitting Member of  this House, Shri K.R. Malk'ani, a 
former Member of this House and Shri Murasoli Maran, a former Member of this 
House and a Union Minister. 
1 

RAJYA SABHA [2 December, 2003]  
Shri Lalbuaia passed away on the 6 of June, 2003, at the age of 84 
years. Born at village Champhai, Mizoram in the year 1919, Shri Lalbuaia was 
an active social and political worker. He was Chairman of the Mizo District 
Council from 1965 to 1970. Shri Lalbuaia also worked as an editor of a local 
daily named 'Mizo Arsi'. Shri Lalbuaia started his distinguished legislative 
career with the membership of the A ssam Legislative Assembly in the year 
1952. He was again elected to that Assembly in the years 1962 and 1970. Shri 
Lalbuaia represented the State of Mizoram in this House from July, 1972 to 
July, 1978. In the passing away of Shri Lalbuaia, the country has lost a noted 
political worker. 
Dr. A. Subba Rao passed away on the 14 th of September, 2003, at the 
age of 84 years. Born at Visakhapatnam in October, 1919, Dr. Subba Rao had 
his education at Pachiappa's College and Government College of Indian 
Medicine, Chennai. A medical practitioner by profession, Dr. Subba Rao 
actively participated in the freedom struggle and was imprisoned for three 
months in 1943 for taking part in a protest demonstration against the detention 
of Mahatma Gandhi. Dr. Subba Rao represented the State of Kerala in this 
House from April, 1958 to April, 1964. He was also elected twice to the Kerala 
Legislative Assembly and remained a Member of that Assembly from 1980 to 
1987. He was Minister of Irrigation in th e Government of Kerala from 1980 to 
1982. In the passing away of Dr. Subb a Rao, the country has lost a noted 
social worker and a freedom fighter. 
Shri K.M. Khan passed away on the 16 th of October, 2003, at the age of 
64 years. Born at Hyderabad, in October 1940, Shri Khan had his education at 
Asafia High School and Mumtaz Coll ege, Hyderabad. A businessman by 
profession, Shri Khan was actively associated with trade union activities. He 
was Secretary of the Indian National Trade Union Congress of the State of 
Andhra Pradesh from 1968 to 1978 and President of the Indian National 
Chemical Workers' Federation from 1973 to 1976. He served as President of 
the Andhra Pradesh Women's Football Association and Global Legislators 
Organization for Balanced Environment. He was also Chairman of the Indo-
Arab Islamic Association and Internatio nal Organisation for Peace, Friendship 
and Human Rights. Shri Khan took keen interest in international affairs, human 
rights, minority welfare, tourism, sports and environment. Shri K.M. Khan 
represented the State of Andhra Pradesh in this House from April, 1994 to 
April, 2000, and, again from April, 2000 till his death. A widely travelled person, 
Shri Khan was Leader and Member of various  Indian  Parliamentary 
delegations and represented the country in 
2  

[2 December, 2003] RAJYA SABHA  
several international events. He led the delegation to the United Nations 
NGOs' Programme at New York in 19 92, and was also leader of an NGO 
delegation to the United Nations. In the passing away of Shri K.M. Khan, the 
country has lost a noted Parliamentarian and an active trade unionist. 
Shri K.R. Malkani passed away on the 27 th of October, 2003, at the 
age of 82 years following cardiac arrest. Born at Hyderabad, Sindh (now in 
Pakistan), in November, 1921, Shri Malkani had his education at Hyderabad, 
Pune, Karachi and Mumbai. 
A teacher and journalist by vocation, Shri Malkani was associated 
with various social and political organisations. He was Vice-President of the 
Deendayal Research Institute, New Delh i from 1983 to 1990 and Bharatiya 
Janata Party from 1990 to 1995. Shri Ma lkani also served as editor / sub-
editor of several leading dailies and weeklies and was General Secretary of 
the Editors Guild of India from 1977 to 1978. 
Shri Malkani represented the National Capital Territory of Delhi in this 
House from April, 1994 to April, 2000. As a Member, Shri Malkani took active 
interest in the proceedings of the House and  made significant contribution. 
Shri Malkani was Lt. Governor of the Union Territory of Pondicherry from July, 
2003 till he breathed his last. 
In the passing away of Shri Malkani,  the country has lost an eminent 
Parliamentarian, a distinguished journalist and an able administrator. 
Shri Murasoli Maran passed away on the 23 ,d of November, 2003 at 
the age of 70 years. Born at village Thir ukkuvalai, District Tanjavur in August, 
1934, Shri Maran had his education at Pachaiyappa's College and Law 
College, Chennai. 
A journalist, political and social worker, Shri Maran since his student 
days was associated with the Dravidian movement. He was also author and 
screen play Wright and wrote dialogues fo r more than twenty Tamil films. He 
was honoured by the Sangeet Natak Academy in the year 1975 for his 
contribution to screenplay and dialogue writing. Shri Maran's films 'Kula 
Deivam' and 'Annayin Aanai' were awarde d President's Certificate of Merit as 
the best and second best regional feat ure films in the years 1956 and 1958, 
respectively. In 1970, his film 'Engal Thangam' got Tamil Nadu Government's 
award for the second best feature film of the year. 
3 

RAJYA SABHA [2 December, 2003]  
Shri Maran was Editor of the Tamil daily 'Murasoli' and the English 
weekly 'The Rising Sun'. He was publisher of several large selling Tamil 
magazines. Shri Maran also had several books on politics and short story 
collections in Tamil to his credit. He was founder member and first President 
of the Madras Press Club. 
Shri Maran had a long and distinguished political career. He was 
Member of Fourth, Fifth, Eleventh, Twelfth and Thirteenth Lok Sabha. Shri 
Maran represented the St ate of Tamil Nadu in this House for three 
consecutive terms from July, 1977 to July, 1983, from July, 1983 to July, 1989, 
and, again from July, 1989 to July, 1995. He was leader of the DMK Party in 
the Rajya Sabha. Shri Maran also served as a Union Minister for several years 
and held the portfolios of Urban Development, Commerce and Industry. As 
Union Commerce and Industry Minister, Shri Maran was in the international 
limelight when he stood up for the causes  of the developing nations in the 
WTO's Doha Summit. 
A widely travelled person, Shri Maran was a Member of the Indian 
Parliamentary Delegation to Commonwealth Parliamentary Conference, 
London, in the year 1989. He was al so a member of the Parliamentary 
delegation to Germany and Ireland in the year 1994. 
In the passing away of Shri Maran, the country has lost an eminent 
Parliamentarian, a noted journalist, an able administrator and a versatile 
personality. 
We deeply mourn the passing away of Shri Lalbuaia, Dr. A. Subba Rao, 
.Shri K.M. Khan, Shri K.R. Malkani and Shri Murasoli Maran. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark 
of respect to the memory of the departed souls. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 
MR.  CHAIRMAN:    Secretary-General will convey to the members of the 
bereaved families our sense of profound sorrow and sympathy. 
REFERENCES BY THE CHAIR 
Victims of twin bomb blasts in Mumbai 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, it is with utmost grief and sorrow 
that I refer to the tragic killing of 52 people and injury to many others in twin 
4 

[2 December, 2003] RAJYA SABHA  
bomb blasts that occurred at the crowded Zaveri Bazar and near Gateway of 
India in Mumbai on 25 th August, 2003. No words are strong enough to condemn 
this heinous act. The killing of so many innocent people has shocked the entire 
nation. I am sure that the whole House wi ll join me in condemning this cowardly 
and senseless act and in offering condolences to the bereaved families and 
expressing concern and sympathy for those who got injured. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of 
respect to the memory of those who lost their lives in this tragedy. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 
Victims of Kumbh Meia stampede in Nashik 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, as you are already aware, a great 
tragedy took place on the 27 th August, 2003, when 29 pilgrims including women 
were killed and several others got injur ed in a stampede during the Kumbh Mela 
in Nashik. The loss of so many preci ous lives has shocked the whole country. 
The loss suffered by the kith and kin of the deceased is irreparable. Our hearts 
go out in sympathy for the bereaved and  we express our concern and sympathy 
for those who got injured. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of 
respect to the memory of those who lost their lives in this tragedy. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 
MR. CHAIRMAN: As a mark of respec t to the memory of Shri K.M. 
Khan, a sitting Member of this House, the House stands adjourned till 11.00 a.m. 
on Wednesday, the 3rd December 2003. 
The House then adjourned at twenty-one minutes past eleven of the clock till 
eleven of the clock on Wednesday, the 3rd December 2003.
